messages:
Ravi Kapoor: Quick one from my trip to Tokyo. My corp card was declined at the telecom kiosk so I bought a local eSIM (data only) for \u00a53,400 on my personal card to stay connected. The store gave an email receipt and QR activation but no VAT invoice. Can I get reimbursed for the eSIM + the prepay top-up I did later?
Maria Gomez: Thanks for flagging. We reimburse necessary telecom expenses for business travel (data/roaming) but need proof of purchase. Please attach the vendor email receipt and your personal card statement line. If the vendor doesn't provide an invoice, a screenshot of the eSIM order/activation with amount + bank line is acceptable.
Ravi Kapoor: Uploaded the emailed receipt and a screenshot of the in-app activation showing the amount. Also have the bank transaction screenshot. I noticed the payment included a small local convenience fee \u00a550 for card terminal. Do we reimburse that too?
Travel Ops: For connectivity purchased because corp card unavailable, we usually reimburse the base service cost and unavoidable vendor surcharges (terminal fees) if documented. Personal card FX/issuer convenience fees are not reimbursed unless the corp card could not be used and there was no other option. Please add a short note "Corp card chip error at kiosk / attempted corp payment" and include last 4 digits of corp card used.
Ravi Kapoor: Note added to expense form. Also curious about monthly plans vs single-use eSIMs: I bought a 30-day plan because it was the only option. Is that ok or do I need pre-approval?
Maria Gomez: Good question. Policy: recurring telecom subscriptions require pre-approval. One-off travel data purchases (multi-day eSIM for trip duration) are reimbursable if documented. If you buy a multi-month plan that exceeds trip length, we reimburse only the prorated portion unless pre-approved. Please put the trip dates in your note so we can prorate.
Manager - Lina: I approve reimbursement for Ravi's eSIM prorated to trip dates (2026-03-10 to 2026-03-17). Lina (manager) approved in expense workflow.
Ravi Kapoor: Thanks Lina. The 30-day plan cost \u00a53,400 and my trip was 8 days. Prorated amount ~\u00a51434. I'll mark prorated amount in the expense and attach justification.
Maria Gomez: Perfect. Submit expense with: 1) vendor email receipt, 2) bank statement line, 3) activation screenshot, 4) manager approval (done), and 5) short prorate calculation in the note. We'll reimburse the prorated service cost and the vendor terminal fee \u00a550 but not your card issuer FX markup. Finance Bot will paste policy link.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: "Temporary travel connectivity (eSIMs, local SIMs, short-term data plans) are reimbursable when used for business travel. Recurring subscriptions need pre-approval. Reimbursement covers actual vendor charges and documented vendor fees; personal card FX/convenience fees are not reimbursed unless corporate card was unavailable and no alternative existed. Required docs: vendor receipt, payment evidence, trip dates, manager approval for prorating. https://intranet.redwood/fin/telecom-reimbursements"
Ravi Kapoor: Submitted expense EXP-1912 with attachments and prorate calc. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: I'll review and process. If anything missing I'll ping you, otherwise expect reimbursement in next cycle.
